info.name: VibeMail API
info.description:
# VibeMail API

Generated from `CONTRACT.md` (endpoints in section 3, shared errors in section 1.5). Every request has a test script, and every error code in the contract has a request.

## Run it locally with no Google account (fake mode)

1. Start the app with `VIBEMAIL_FAKES=1`, `JWT_SECRET` and `FRONTEND_URL` set, for example `npx vercel dev` (the first run needs a linked Vercel project). Fake mode serves 60 demo messages for `demo@vibemail.test` and never leaves the process. Production refuses to start with it.
2. Leave `baseUrl` as `http://localhost:3000` (or change it) and set `frontendUrl` to the server's `FRONTEND_URL`.
3. Optional, for the requests that need them: set `jwtSecret` to the server's `JWT_SECRET` and `webhookToken` to its `GOOGLE_PUBSUB_VERIFICATION_TOKEN`.
4. Run the collection **in order** (Collection Runner). Folder 1 and 2 sign in and set `{{jwt}}`; folder 3 sets `{{messageId}}`, `{{threadId}}` and `{{rfc822MessageId}}` for the folders after it.

## Against real Google

Sign in with a browser (`GET {{baseUrl}}/api/v1/auth/google`), copy the `token` from the redirect's URL fragment into `{{jwt}}`, and skip folder 2's happy path. **The send happy paths send real email, and marking read changes a real mailbox.**

## Variables

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `baseUrl` | `http://localhost:3000` | The server |
| `frontendUrl` | `http://localhost:3001` | The server's `FRONTEND_URL`, where sign-in redirects |
| `jwt` | empty | Session token, set by the callback happy path |
| `oauthState` | empty | The sign-in `state`, set by the start request |
| `fakeAuthCode` | `fake-authorization-code` | The fixed code the fake consent URL returns (fake mode only) |
| `messageId`, `threadId`, `rfc822MessageId`, `pageToken` | empty | Set by the list request |
| `mailboxEmail` | `demo@vibemail.test` | The signed-in mailbox the webhook notifies about |
| `webhookToken` | empty | The webhook's shared secret |
| `jwtSecret` | empty | **Local testing only.** Forges tokens for the `GMAIL_REAUTH_REQUIRED` requests. Never put a production secret in a shared or synced collection. |

## Error requests that a client cannot trigger

Some contract errors depend on Gmail or the database failing (`GMAIL_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT`, `GMAIL_RATE_LIMITED`, `GMAIL_UPSTREAM_ERROR`, `INTERNAL`, `INVALID_RECIPIENT`, `PERSISTENCE_FAILED`, and `OAUTH_MISSING_SCOPES` / `OAUTH_NO_REFRESH_TOKEN`, which only Google's consent screen causes). They still have a request, named "(not triggerable)", with a saved example response showing the documented envelope. Their tests assert only when the condition actually occurs, and are skipped otherwise.

## Notes

- Errors use `{ "error": { "code", "message", "details?", "retryAfterSeconds?" } }`. The OAuth callback is the exception: it is a browser redirect and reports failures as `?error=<CODE>`.
- The contract's names are `UNAUTHENTICATED` (not UNAUTHORIZED) and `VALIDATION_FAILED` (not MISSING_FIELDS).
- Mark-as-read is `POST`, not `PATCH`.

item.name: 1. Sign-in start: GET /api/v1/auth/google
item.description:
CONTRACT 3.1 (start). No JWT. Creates a random `state`, stores it in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure cookie for 10 minutes, and redirects (302) to Google's consent screen with `access_type=offline` and `prompt=consent`. Redirects are not followed so you can see the `Location` and `Set-Cookie` headers.

**Run this first.** Its test script saves `state` into `{{oauthState}}` for the callback requests. With `VIBEMAIL_FAKES=1` the `Location` points straight back at the callback with a fixed fake code.

The start route has no error codes of its own.

request.description: Expected: 302 with `Location` (the consent URL, carrying `state`) and a `Set-Cookie` for `vibemail_oauth_state`.

exec: const param = (text, name) => { const m = new RegExp("[?&#]" + name + "=([^&#]*)").exec(text); return m ? decodeURIComponent(m[1]) : null; };
pm.test("Location carries a state nonce", () => pm.expect(param(location, "state")).to.match(/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/));
pm.test("State cookie is HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax and lasts 10 minutes", () => {

item.name: 2. OAuth callback: GET /api/v1/auth/google/callback
item.description:
CONTRACT 3.1 (callback). No JWT. Google redirects the browser here with `code`, `state` and `scope`. On success the browser is redirected to `{{frontendUrl}}/auth/callback#token=<JWT>` (the token is in the URL fragment); every failure is a 302 to `{{frontendUrl}}/login?error=<CODE>`.

Run `1. Sign-in start` first so `{{oauthState}}` is set. The happy path below completes the flow automatically **only against a server running with `VIBEMAIL_FAKES=1`**; against real Google, complete the consent screen in a browser instead and paste the token from the redirect into `{{jwt}}`.

item.name: 4. Send message: POST /api/v1/messages/send
item.description: CONTRACT 3.3. JWT required. Builds the message, sends it once through Gmail, reads it back and stores the sent copy. Body: `to` (1 to 100 `{name?, email}`), `cc?`, `bcc?`, `subject` (0 to 998 chars, no line breaks), `bodyText?` and/or `bodyHtml?` (at least one), and for a reply `threadId` together with `inReplyTo` (all or nothing), optional `references`. **Sending is not idempotent: re-running a successful request sends another email.**

item.name: Happy path: new message (text and HTML)

request.description:

item.name: 6. Pub/Sub webhook: POST /webhook/gmail
item.description: CONTRACT 3.5. Not under /api/v1. Called by a Pub/Sub push subscription, not by a browser, so there is no JWT and no CORS. It is authenticated by the shared secret in `?token=` (`GOOGLE_PUBSUB_VERIFICATION_TOKEN`, the `webhookToken` variable). `message.data` is base64 JSON `{ emailAddress, historyId }`; the `historyId` is validated and ignored, because the delta resumes from the stored cursor. Pub/Sub treats any 2xx as an acknowledgement and retries everything else. Served at `/webhook/gmail` through a `vercel.json` rewrite.

**Expected: 429 `GMAIL_RATE_LIMITED`.** Gmail throttled the delta fetch. Pub/Sub treats the non-2xx as a failure and redelivers; the history cursor has not advanced. A client cannot cause this on demand.

This is the happy-path request; the saved example shows the documented response.

Called by a Pub/Sub push subscription, not by a browser, so there is no JWT and no CORS. It is authenticated by the shared secret in `?token=` (`GOOGLE_PUBSUB_VERIFICATION_TOKEN`, the `webhookToken` variable). `message.data` is base64 JSON `{ emailAddress, historyId }`; the `historyId` is validated and ignored, because the delta resumes from the stored cursor. Pub/Sub treats any 2xx as an acknowledgement and retries everything else. Served at `/webhook/gmail` through a `vercel.json` rewrite.
